competitive_landscape: The water today is served by RTA abras, water buses, water taxis and ferries, plus private yacht charter. Abras are slow and short-hop; the water-taxi network is thin and premium-priced; there is no fast, frequent point-to-point network linking Marina, Palm, Harbour and Creek. The road network — not the water — carries the traffic, and it is chronically gridlocked. That gap is the demand.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Runs multi-rotation days on a single charge across Marina ↔ Palm ↔ Harbour ↔ Creek with no new charging infrastructure beyond a home-berth pedestal. Sheltered inner waters are ideal first-of-class operating conditions.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Collapses the previously out-of-reach Gulf corridors — Abu Dhabi, Sir Bani Yas, Khasab, Muscat, Doha, Manama — into routine single-leg corridors, with no charging-infrastructure dependency (hybrid refuel + near-silent electric on approach).

regulatory_note: Marine activity falls under RTA marine licensing and the Dubai Maritime City Authority, within Dubai's Net-Zero-2050 and clean-energy agenda — a zero-emission premium fleet aligns directly with stated policy. (Authority engagement to be coordinated at leadership level.)
seasonality: Inner waters (Marina, Palm, Creek, Harbour) are sheltered and operable year-round. Summer (Jun–Sep) is hot but calm; winter shamal winds bring short chop that foiling rides smoothly. Peak visitor season is Oct–Apr.
signature_routes: Dubai Marina ↔ Palm ↔ Dubai Harbour (all-electric inner network)

summary: Dubai is the rare market where all five marine-mobility use cases coexist within a 20 nm radius: a sheltered network of creek, canals and man-made islands made for routine all-electric hops, plus an open-Gulf opportunity that long-range hybrids turn into single-leg corridors. Roads are congested; the water is empty.
tagline: The world's most ambitious waterfront — gridlocked on land, wide open on water.
transit_planning: For a transport authority: Navier adds a premium, zero-emission foiling layer on top of the existing marine network — new high-value corridors (Creek premium, Dubai↔Abu Dhabi express) and a credible decarbonization path for water-bus/ferry renewal — while leaving the abra cooperative untouched as a protected heritage trade.

use_cases.body: MENA demand already lives inside the super-app. A foiling water tier — booked in-app, premium pricing — turns Marina, Harbour, Palm and Creek into on-demand water routes without touching the protected abra trade.
